item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-09
item.description: On 2026-08-28, at Huawei's HarmonyOS Ecosystem Conference in Shenzhen, OpenAtom Foundation chairman Xie Shaofeng stated that the foundation will spend 150 million yuan a year for the next three years on root-technology evolution, shared industrial capability, toolchains, security, compatibility testing and key technology, and reported OpenHarmony's totals: 140 million-plus lines of code, 13,808 contributors, 644 community partners, 53 project-group donors, 2,040-plus compatible products across 23 technical domains, 11 releases over six years, graduated in 2025. Read against the foundation's own governance description — a neutral platform holding code and brand as public assets, with a layered governance structure covering strategy, technical planning and version R&D — those two paragraphs describe a different institution from the one a Western foundation is. The second half of this briefing measures that institution on a project it already holds: PikiwiDB, donated by Qihoo 360 and published under OpenAtomFoundation/pikiwidb, which carries 6,136 stars and 1,170 forks, has 1,716 pull requests and 1,379 issues in its history, merged 584 of 800 enumerated pull requests, and in 2026 has taken 31 commits from five named authors, 22 of them from a single @360.cn address and 3 from a Copilot account. Twelve issues opened since 2026-10-01 sit with zero comments. Its MAINTAINERS.md names three maintainers, exactly one of whom lists an employer, and that employer is 360. The foundation now has a budget of 150 million yuan a year and a project with 12,000 stars whose October went unanswered — and the distance between those two facts is the binding constraint this series has been tracking since July.
